docker_scenario.topology: 1 server + peer-a + peer-b on an isolated internal bridge, real crypto/binaries built with the pq-dev-harness feature, fake kernel installer only
bugs_found_and_fixed_by_this_milestone: engine.rs's per-message absorb loop couldn't find the counterparty's final message once Exchange::compact() cleared it on a terminal record, so a side that fell one poll behind would never observe completion -- fixed by adopting the exchange's own still-present terminal Decision wholesale once terminal, instead of replaying individual messages

the durable-send retry check trusted a locally-optimistic terminal decision as proof of durability, letting a side falsely declare victory when its own final message (e.g. its Confirmed receipt) was the one actually lost -- fixed by keying trust off the server's own reported Exchange.decision, which can only reach a terminal phase once every required message was truly processed

limitations: Real WireGuard installation/handshake observation is not implemented (FakeInstaller only); that is M4's job

The Docker scenario exercises one rotation with a freshly generated identity per container; re-rotation of the *same* established identity producing a different candidate is covered by pq/src/engine.rs's own unit tests, not through real containers
Proactive client-initiated Abort is not implemented (the engine only observes one, whether peer-signed or TTL-expired); sending one is policy/M6 territory
The tunnel-inactivity/idle-timeout pause scheduling that will reuse this driver loop is M5

--pq-psk-rotation-interval is validated and consumed by the engine, but no CLI path yet threads a live client's flag value into a running up --daemon loop, since that loop's own PQ wiring stays behind --enable-pq-psk's production refusal until M4
